_coverage.title: Never call pause_reminders and opt_out in the same turn.

name: user explicitly unsubscribes with stop
input: I mean it, don’t text me again for anything.

conversation.content: Hi Jordan, this is Robin from Bramblewood Clinic. Want to set up your annual physical sometime this month?
No. Stop texting me about anything, unsubscribe this number.

grading_criteria:
The assistant should recognize this as a clear opt-out request and:
- Call opt_out exactly once with a reason reflecting that the user asked to stop all texts / unsubscribe.
- Not call pause_reminders in this turn.
- Not attempt any scheduling, lookups, or other actions.
- Reply briefly confirming that texting will stop and that they can contact the clinic directly if needed.
The key point is that only opt_out, not pause_reminders, is used, honoring the rule against calling both in the same turn.

checks.opt_out_called: Did the assistant call opt_out with a reason indicating the user requested to stop all texts?
checks.pause_not_called: Did the assistant avoid calling pause_reminders in this turn?
checks.no_scheduling_actions: Did the assistant avoid any booking/rescheduling/cancel tools in this turn?
checks.confirmation_text_sent: Did the assistant send a short confirmation that texts will stop, without arguing or trying to retain the user?

opt_out.reason: User explicitly requested to stop all texts and unsubscribe this number.
